The INR 65 crore order book (executing by Sep-26) and a INR 200+ crore quoted pipeline provide high visibility for crossing INR 100 crore revenue in FY27 and targeting INR 200 crore by FY28.

hero.industry: Defense & Nuclear Inspection Systems / Steel Processing Automation

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Steel (Long products ~70-75%, Flat ~25-30%): Chamfering, straightening, bright bar finishing; Defense: X-ray/NDT for missile shells (155mm Howitzer), aerospace components; Nuclear: Fuel handling systems (NFC orders); Exports: 28 countries, direct to US (6 pipe projects) and Brazil/Taiwan/Korea defense deals.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR 65 crores total; Includes INR 10cr from Nuclear Fuel Complex (execution by Sep-26); Mixed bag across Steel, Defense, Nuclear, Packaging; Current dispatches delayed slightly due to global shipping constraints (resolved via South Africa route).

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue: Cross INR 100cr in FY27, target INR 200cr by FY28; Margin: Target >20% EBITDA in FY27 driven by backward integration; Order Inflow: INR 200cr+ quoted pipeline with 60-65% conversion expected; Capex: Near completion, final machines arriving July 2026.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into 'Bright Bar' and superfinishing equipment (downstream of rolling mills); Pre-rolling billet conditioning lines (partnership with Braun Machinefabrik, Austria) adding INR 30-40cr potential per plant vs INR 50cr post-rolling; Nuclear pipeline of 4-8 additional projects beyond current INR 10cr order; Direct exports under own brand increasing vs partner-led.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin compressed to 29% (from 33%) due to project mix shift away from high-margin steel projects (Tata Steel FY24) to diversified base; Backward integration (CNC laser, press brake, tapping) shifting outsourcing ratio from 70/30 to 30/70 (in-house), expected to add 300-400 bps to EBITDA margins starting Q1 FY27.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Organic capacity expansion prioritized; Working capital requirement estimated at INR 20-30cr for INR 200cr revenue scale; No M&A mentioned; Focus on reducing job-work payouts to improve cash conversion.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Highly confident on growth trajectory ('sky is the limit'); Transparent about margin dip being temporary (commissioning phase); Aggressive on defense/nuclear opportunities citing 'Make in India' mandates; Pragmatic on logistics challenges with solutions implemented.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Execution risk on large single-order dispatches (INR 15-16cr units) impacting quarterly lumpiness; Receivable days elevated (150-160 days) due to logistics/shipping delays rather than customer credit, though cash flow timing affected; Dependency on government capex cycles (Defense/Nuclear/Steel); Project-based revenue recognition leading to volatility.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Revenue recognition tied strictly to dispatch (ex-works), causing inventory-to-revenue lumps; Tax rate anomaly (9% H2 vs 25% historical) clarified as benefit from accelerated depreciation on new capex under IT Act, not cash withholding; Defense applications include full-shell X-ray inspection for live ammunition (Brazil/Taiwan/Korea exports), a high-barrier niche; 'Bright Bar' demand driven by automotive shift away from black bars.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for indigenous inspection of missile shells and nuclear fuel components | Admach Systems Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of defense indigenization and nuclear capex; sole domestic player with export credentials in high-kV X-ray for defense. |
| Steel mills expanding capacity and moving downstream to value-added bright bars | Tata Steel | beneficiary | Med | Customer expanding capacity; Admach provides critical finishing lines, though Tata Steel is a customer not a peer beneficiary. |
| Global supply chain constraints delaying capital equipment delivery | Indian Steel & Defense OEMs | loser | Low | Delays in receiving Admach machines due to shipping constraints could delay their own commissioning, though Admach has found alternative routes. |
